sections.h2: Where the Register of Deeds is and what it does
sections.html:
The office is at 170 NC Hwy 65, Suite 150, Reidsville, NC 27320. Phone 336-342-8820, fax 336-342-6209. It is open weekdays, and it takes documents for recording until 4:30 p.m. on days the county is open.

Staff describe the office as a recording agency. They do not draft documents, fill in forms or search title, so a Rockingham County seller normally relies on a closing attorney to prepare the deed and carry it to the counter. For any question about legal forms, consult an attorney.

sections.h2: What a deed needs before it will be recorded
sections.html:
The office posts a checklist, and a deed that skips an item can be refused or hit with an added fee. These items matter most in a house sale:

  • Page one names whoever drafted the deed, a person or a law firm.
  • Page one also carries the buyer's mailing address, because the tax office uses it for billing.
  • Notarized papers show the acknowledgment, the notary's official seal and the date that commission ends.
  • Conveyances show the excise stamp amount on their face. If nothing is owed, the signer writes NTC, short for no taxable consideration.
  • No Social Security, bank account, card, passport or license numbers may appear, except the final four digits where the law demands an identifier.
  • Mail-ins need a check or money order to the Rockingham County Register of Deeds and a return envelope with a stamp. A bounced check costs $25.

Your attorney usually handles all of this, but check it yourself on a family deed, a deed into a trust, or a sale with no attorney.

Rockingham County enforces the statewide standard in G.S. 161-14, and a document that misses it picks up a $25 surcharge. The standards call for letter or legal paper, black ink on white, a clear three-inch strip across the top of the first sheet and a quarter inch of white space around everything else.

Beneath that strip, page one states what kind of instrument it is. Print must be nine points or larger and appear on a single side. Pen may fill blanks or make corrections. Satisfactions, cancellations, military discharges and separately recorded plats (governed by G.S. 47-30) are exempt. The register may overlook a slightly small font if it copies cleanly, but stay above nine points.

The county's fee page tracks the state statute and adds practical items such as copies. These lines matter to a house seller:

Selected Rockingham County Register of Deeds fees
ServiceFee
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for 35 pages, then $4.00 per page or fraction
Multiple instruments in one document$10.00 for each added instrument
Parties above 20 in one instrument$2.00 for each extra party
SatisfactionsNo fee
State excise tax on conveyances$2.00 per thousand ($1.00 up to $500.00)
Certified land record copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 later pages
Uncertified copy$0.25 per page

The same schedule prices passports, marriage licenses and vital records, which have no bearing on a sale. Plat copies of 18 by 24 inches or larger run $3.00 a page uncertified.

sections.h2: How the deed excise tax is figured
sections.html:
Divide the sale price into $500 slices and charge $1 per slice, counting a partial slice as a whole one. A price that lands between two $500 marks is rounded up to the next one before the math.

The grantor reports and pays the tax at the register before the deed is accepted, so it normally appears among the seller's charges at settlement. The county keeps half of the revenue in its general fund and passes the rest to the state. Ask your closing attorney for the figure before the closing date, so there are no surprises on the settlement statement. If the deed carries NTC, no stamp amount is owed.

The office processes in-person filings first, then e-recordings, then priority mail such as UPS or FedEx, then regular mail. Each item has to be opened, reviewed and found acceptable before it is recorded.

The 4:30 p.m. cutoff applies to paper and electronic filings alike. Anyone already in line at 4:30 is served that day. Later arrivals wait until another day. If the exact recording date carries real weight, hand the instrument over at the counter and stay until it is recorded.

E-recording is accepted during business hours. It has three benefits: the recorded document comes back right away, nobody has to travel, and a rejection is flagged immediately. Ask the office for its list of approved e-recording vendors.

sections.h2: Looking up land records and mortgage releases
sections.html:
The E-Vault is the county's public search site for land records. For 1789 through 1995 the official index is the paper index inside the office, with scanned copies under an Old Index Books tab. From 1996 on, the electronic database in the office is the official index. Vital records are not in the E-Vault, and website records are unofficial, so the office holds the official set.

Fresh filings appear first in a temporary index shown in red entries and move to the permanent index, in blue, after full indexing. Use fewer characters in the search fields for better results.

When a loan is paid off, the lender must file a satisfaction. Recording a satisfaction is free, but reference only one original instrument per satisfaction to avoid a $25 charge for each extra reference. A payoff does not create a new deed. You can pull a copy of the satisfaction from the E-Vault or at the office.

Confirm that every old loan shows a recorded satisfaction and that the vesting deed matches the name on the contract. A missing release is the most common snag, and a buyer's title insurer will ask for it.

  • Search the E-Vault for the last deed and any deed of trust on the parcel.
  • Ask the lender about any loan paid off years ago with no release showing.
  • Confirm that the grantee's mailing address and the drafter's name are on the deed.
  • Ask the attorney whether the deed goes by e-recording or in person at Reidsville.

Under North Carolina law a deed carries no weight against later buyers or lien creditors until it is on the record of the county holding the parcel, and rank follows registration time. That is why buyers push for same-day recording after funds move.

faqs.q: When should I arrive to record a deed in Rockingham County?
faqs.a: Arrive before 4:30 p.m. on a weekday. That is when the office stops taking documents for recording, and a later arrival is not recorded that day.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a mortgage satisfaction in Rockingham County?
faqs.a: No, recording a satisfaction is free. The county charges $25 for each extra reference when one satisfaction document points to more than one original instrument, so list only one.

faqs.q: Does Rockingham County accept recording by mail?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the original with a check or money order to the Rockingham County Register of Deeds plus a stamped return envelope, never cash. Regular mail is handled after in-person, electronic and priority-mail items.

faqs.q: How is the deed excise tax calculated in Rockingham County?
faqs.a: The seller pays $1 per $500 of price, rounding up to the next $500. It is paid at the register before the deed is accepted.

faqs.q: Does the Rockingham County register of deeds search title for me?
faqs.a: No. The office is a recording agency and cannot help complete forms or run a title search. Hire an attorney or title agent for that, and use the E-Vault for your own look at the record.
